tweets.full_text: @x-user-1 Show horse vs workhorse is the right split. Demo latency and tasteful diffs win the timeline. Day to day product work wants a model that survives half-written specs, flaky tests, and the third retry without turning theatrical. Fun is not the same as shippable.

Flaky tests are worse than no tests. Once a suite cries wolf enough times, nobody reads the red anymore.

#BuildInPublic #SoftwareTesting #QA

300 SUB-AGENTS. ZERO AUTO-MERGES.

That is how you build a serious 24/7 repo operations desk.

Kimi K3 can coordinate the parallel swarm and hold up to one million tokens of context.

Grok Build can inspect code, run tests, edit files, and operate inside CI.

Split the system into six roles:

TRIAGE sorts every issue.
FIX touches only bounded failures.
TEST hunts flaky suites.
DEPENDENCY watches CVEs.
RELEASE prepares changelogs.
ALERT wakes the human when the blast radius is real.

Lint, formatting, and known flaky tests can become draft PRs.

Application logic, critical security changes, and every production merge remain behind a human gate.

The goal is not replacing the engineer.

It is replacing the engineer who checks CI at 2AM because nobody else is watching.

Watch everything.
Fix only what is bounded.
Escalate everything dangerous.

@x-user-35 @x-user-36 Hit this with a per-seat reviewer last month. Cheap model started rubber-stamping flaky tests. Switched to BYOK + one SOTA call on the dirty files only.
@x-user-46 Deterministic tests for agent tool usage is a great idea. LLM based evals are so flaky run to run, having a non LLM harness for the tool call logic itself makes debugging way faster.

XAI ENGINEERS JUST SHOWED WHAT A 24/7 REPO OPS DESK COULD LOOK LIKE WITH GROK BOT

grok bot can watch ci, tests, dependencies and security signals continuously instead of waiting for someone to notice a broken repo hours later

6 bots → 300 repo monitors → 60-second checks → triage → safe patch → draft pr → human review

flaky tests, lint and deterministic failures stay inside the safe lane. regressions, cves and anything touching real logic get routed straight back to a person

the system can wait for 3 clean runs, track a 95% test threshold and prepare the fix with context, but it never merges code on its own

this is the shift from manually checking repos all day to letting grok bot run the night shift while humans keep the final decision

Isolate workers. Seed via APIs. Clean up deterministically.

@x-user-132 spent 8 months at an old job just deleting dead code and fixing flaky tests. nobody clapped, but deploys went from weekly and terrifying to ten a day.

Everyone talks about the test pyramid, but few follow it.

Here's what actually happens:

❌ 70% UI tests (slow, flaky)
❌ 20% integration tests
❌ 10% unit tests

Flip it:
✅ 70% unit tests (fast, reliable)
✅ 20% integration tests
✅ 10% UI tests (critical paths only)

Speed beats coverage if coverage slows you down.
